clue.text: From roundabout, river on vehicle's left

indicators.note: in an across clue, the river sitting on the vehicle means it comes after it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle; the possessive adds no letter
the Ouse is a river in England (there are several of the name)

explanation.surface: Directions for leaving a traffic roundabout, with a river on the vehicle's left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' looks like a road junction but means a fairground merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground roundabout or merry-go-round is the same ride as a carousel, a synonym.

clue.text: Finished very characteristically

definitions.meaning: something finished is ended and done with
as in 'that's him ...', meaning typical of someone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both ended completely and, idiomatically, exactly typical of a person.

clue.text: Get down to the start of the course

definitions.text: Get down to the start of the course

parts.words: Get down to the start of the course
parts.note: read as a starter's order: runners crouch down at the starting line of a race course

explanation.definitionFit: The starter's command tells sprinters to crouch at the starting line before a race begins.

clue.text: Make a film of country sport

definitions.meaning: to film a scene is to capture it on camera
a day's game-bird hunting on an estate, a traditional British country pursuit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to film something and also a hunting party for game birds on an estate.

clue.text: Skin condition has spread into leg

indicators.note: letters that have spread out are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rash on the skin has crept down into someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has spread' rearranges the seven letters of INTO LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a medical term for a small flat brown patch on the skin, a freckle-like condition.

clue.text: Recommending parking away from clearing

indicators.note: parking is taken away from the word for clearing

parts.note: purging is clearing out or cleansing
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone advising that cars be kept away from a cleared area.
explanation.definitionFit: Urging someone to do something is strongly advising or recommending it, a synonym.

clue.text: Raised havoc — always raised at a winter festival

parts.note: up means raised, as a hand is up
hell means chaos or havoc, as in 'all hell broke loose'

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ay (aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Revellers stirring up trouble, as they always do, at a midwinter celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'raised' turns AY into YA. Up Helly Aa is the Shetland fire festival held each January, where a Viking galley is burned.
explanation.definitionFit: Up Helly Aa is a famous Shetland fire festival held in midwinter, an example of the category.

clue.text: Semi-solid support taken up

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A soft jelly-like support is lifted into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A gel is a jelly-like substance between liquid and solid, a semi-solid by nature.

clue.text: What's needed after rioters broke out of this prison?

definitions.text: What's needed after rioters broke out of this prison?

parts.words: What's needed after rioters broke out of this prison?
parts.note: once escaping rioters have smashed the prison entrance, a replacement entrance must be fitted

explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was the notorious London prison, and the name read literally describes a replacement entrance.

clue.text: Be dogmatic, as judge will when he retires

definitions.meaning: to insist on one's opinions without allowing argument

definitions.text: as judge will when he retires
definitions.meaning: a retiring judge literally puts down his legal role, giving up the law

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to state rules dogmatically, and read literally a retiring judge gives up the law.

clue.text: Leave once with a boast

parts.note: to vaunt is to boast or brag

explanation.surface: Someone departs from a group with a final brag.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an old command meaning go away, so it is a former way of telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Mismanage doctor's job, getting parts in wrong order

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase swap places, the back half moving to the front

parts.note: a doctor's job is to treat the ill, the sick

explanation.surface: A doctor botches a job by doing things in the wrong sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: TREAT ILL has ILL moved from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat is to handle badly or abuse, so it is a synonym for mishandling someone.

clue.text: Wave, not seeing what may be at the window

definitions.text: what may be at the window

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy sea wave
blind means unable to see

explanation.surface: Someone waves at a window without being able to see anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like a verb but is a noun for a breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller blind is a window covering that rolls up, so it may well hang at the window.

clue.text: Point to railway and walk on ahead

indicators.note: the walk and the word on are placed ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a prom (promenade) is a seaside walk
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions: point towards the railway line and keep walking straight on.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland jutting into the sea, and a point is another word for such a headland.

clue.text: Only the facts? I wouldn't like to say

definitions.meaning: a report with only facts carries no opinion added by the writer
a refusal to give a view, as a politician might say to the press

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock refusal to give an opinion, and also describes bare facts with no opinion attached.

clue.text: Legal right to put name to perjured statement

parts.note: perjury is telling a lie under oath

explanation.surface: A lawyer claims the right to sign a name on false testimony.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'to' places N after LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Nasty mark that one may have round the neck shortly

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.words: that one may have round the neck
parts.note: a scarf is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A nasty mark left on someone's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals, an unsightly blemish.

clue.text: Man at last getting line almost up for clothes

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter climbs nearly to the top, stopping one short

parts.note: a man working at a last, the shoe-shaped form, mends shoes: a cobbler

explanation.surface: A man finally gets a clothes line almost hung up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like 'finally' but is the shoemaker's last. L moves up from fifth place to second. Clobber is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing or gear, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Pass a line round afterwards for security

indicators.note: the pass, a and line go around the word for afterwards

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: A hint to throw a line around a gap afterwards to make things secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' sends the pass, A and line around the word for afterwards, the first three letters landing in front and the last two behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security for a loan, a financial synonym.

clue.text: Gosh, judge, I'm a hero to some readers

parts.note: 'Lord!' is an exclamation of surprise like gosh
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise from a judge who thinks himself a hero to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Jim is the title character of Joseph Conrad's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Jim is the hero of Joseph Conrad's novel, so a heroic figure to those who read it.

clue.text: From being in the middle, man's got out

indicators.note: letters that are out are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; the possessive's S counts here as fodder

explanation.surface: A man has escaped from being stuck in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MANSGOT; 'got out' reads as escaping.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means surrounded by or in the midst of others, a near-synonym of being in the middle.

clue.text: Fine stuff — order me a gross

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A customer orders a gross of fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a very fine, light, filmy material, so it is delicate stuff.

clue.text: Asia's native historian

definitions.meaning: an ape native to South-East Asia
Edward ... wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a long-armed ape native to Asia and the eighteenth-century historian Edward Gibbon.

clue.text: One having fun with computer? I bet

definitions.meaning: someone who bets or gambles, a gamester

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a player of computer games and, in an older sense, a gambler who places bets.

clue.text: Bounce back after being dropped in this sport

definitions.text: Bounce back after being dropped in this sport

parts.words: Bounce back after being dropped in this sport
parts.note: read as recovering from being dropped from a team, but literally a jumper on an elastic cord springs back up after the fall

explanation.definitionFit: In this activity a person falls from a height on an elastic cord and rebounds upwards.

clue.text: Keep worrying that horse is old

definitions.meaning: to pester someone with constant complaints

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to pester constantly and also an old, broken-down horse.

clue.text: Shock resistance maintained in brawl

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a brawl is a fight
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A brawler gets a shock when the other side keeps up its resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock of fear, a synonym.

clue.text: Man of letters hammered — it hurt a bit

indicators.note: the answer is just a bit of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A writer is attacked and complains that it hurt a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in hamMERED IT Hurt. George Meredith was a Victorian novelist and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith was a Victorian novelist and poet, a writer or literary figure.
